01Why now

Why this course, and why now

Most people learn architecture by absorbing it from the one or two systems they have worked on. This level gives you the shared vocabulary and the working method first: requirements and constraints, structure, patterns, views, evaluation, and how to decide when and how to use AI. It follows the topics of the iSAQB Foundation Level curriculum, so it is also a way to prepare for that exam.

External reference: iSAQB CPSA-F curriculum. The current official curriculum is version 2025.1. iSAQB has published a 2027.1 release candidate scheduled to take effect on 1 April 2027; Intellica will refresh its mapping before that date. This is independent self-study, not iSAQB-accredited training.

02Outcomes

What you will be able to do

Speak the language

Use the core terms correctly: structure, building blocks, views, quality, decisions and the architect’s role.

Find what shapes the design

Separate requirements from constraints, assumptions and preferences, and write quality goals as measurable scenarios.

Design and describe

Decompose a system, choose patterns with reasons, define interfaces, runtime and deployment, and document it in views others can read.

Evaluate and prepare

Test a design with evidence, verify AI-drafted architecture content, and take five timed mock exams with a readiness report.

This level follows the topics of the iSAQB CPSA-F curriculum (version 2025.1). It is Intellica self-study, not an iSAQB course, and Intellica is not an accredited training provider. The exam is booked separately with an iSAQB certification body; training is not required to sit it. Check the current exam format with the certification body before you book.

04The lab

Your architecture file for one system

Pick a system you know, or use the ClinicBook case. After every lesson one lab section adds to a single architecture file: 14 sections in all. The labs are design and writing work with a model solution and a rubric each. A health check confirms the file is complete and free of placeholders and secrets; it does not judge whether your design is right. One file, built in steps after each lesson. Each step has instructions, a model solution and a rubric to mark your own work, and saves on your device.

The steps

  1. Lesson 1: What Software Architecture Is and What Architects Do
  2. Lesson 2: Stakeholders, Requirements and Constraints
  3. Lesson 3: Quality Attributes and Measurable Scenarios
  4. Lesson 4: Design Approaches and Decomposition
  5. Lesson 5: Design Principles and Patterns
  6. Lesson 6: Interfaces, Contracts and Data Models
  7. Lesson 7: Runtime Views and Distributed Systems
  8. Lesson 8: Deployment and Infrastructure
  9. Lesson 9: Cross-Cutting Concepts
  10. Lesson 10: Documenting and Communicating Architecture
  11. Lesson 11: Analysing and Assessing Architecture
  12. Lesson 12: Worked Example: The Integrated Case Study
  13. Lesson 13: AI-Assisted Architecture Work
  14. Lesson 14: Exam Strategy and the Final Mock

What the health check looks for

  • All 14 section headings are present
  • Every section has been started
  • Every task in a started section has a real answer (12 words or more)
  • No placeholder text is left in started sections
  • Quality and analysis sections contain numbers
  • Nothing in the file looks confidential

05How you learn

Evidence-led learning method

Worked examples

The professional academies begin with complete examples and make the reasoning behind good decisions visible.

Guided practice

Scaffolds fade as learners progress—from annotated examples to structured tasks and independent work.

Retrieval and review

Low-stakes questions prompt recall; review revisits important concepts. Model answers and rubrics make improvement specific.

Research-informed updates

The academies cite primary research and standards, record review dates and receive versioned updates as evidence changes.

The method follows published research on retrieval practice, worked examples and spaced review. Read the evidence and sources.

06Certificate

A certificate you can verify and share

After meeting the published course-completion criteria, learners can claim a certificate with its own credential ID and a public verification page. The certificate can be shared or saved as a PDF.

To earn it

  1. Finish every lesson
  2. Complete every lab step and pass its health checks
  3. Answer at least 70% of the check questions correctly, on the first try or in review

What you get

  • A credential ID and a public page that confirms it
  • Add to LinkedIn in one click
  • Share on LinkedIn, X or Facebook, or copy the link
  • Save as a PDF

The certificate records completion against the course rules, based on progress reported by the learner’s browser. It is self-reported and unproctored; lab work is not independently marked by Intellica. It is not accredited as a professional qualification and does not confer or replace an external certification.

07Who it is for

What it builds on

No earlier level. Some experience building or maintaining software helps, and basic UML and object-oriented ideas are assumed.
